<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Dense Qwen3 prefill launches QK normalization and cached RoPE separately, then FA3 or FlashInfer materializes contiguous Q. This change combines normalization, the same cached RoPE, and contiguous Q output in one CUDA launch. K is normalized and rotated in its original packed QKV storage; Q input and V remain unchanged.

It uses the existing `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` opt-in and remains disabled by default on CUDA. Attention kernels and KV-cache handling are unchanged.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- **Kernel:** Add lazily registered `attention.qk_norm_rope` with FP16/BF16 support, tensor/device/dtype/stride/alignment checks, and explicit K/output mutation metadata. D128 processes two rows per warp; D64/D256 use one. Share the existing standalone half-warp normalization arithmetic, round normalized values before FP32-table rotation, and preserve shuffle participation for an unmatched final row.
- **Dense dispatch:** Fuse only ordinary dense-Qwen3 `EXTEND` on Hopper, head dimension 128, TP1, unquantized weights, FA3/FlashInfer, full-head unscaled NeoX RoPE, and matching activation/weight dtypes. Keep speculative, mixed, verification, inherited/non-Qwen3, deterministic, compiled, and other unvalidated configurations on the separate path. Preserve existing BF16 table decode guards.
- **Coverage/documentation:** Extend existing kernel and model fixtures for native byte parity, Q/K/V ownership, padding, empty input, fallback dispatch, and changing-input CUDA graphs. Add a cold-L2 preparation benchmark including the baseline consumer's Q conversion, and document the opt-in in the Qwen3 cookbook.

Disabling the existing flag or reverting this contribution rolls the change back; there is no checkpoint, schema, or persisted-data migration. On upstream base-versus-PR comparisons, keep the existing flag enabled in both trees so BF16 decode treatment is identical.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

**Current contribution-source checks**, run on H200 and the checkout's Python path:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_table_qk_norm_rope.py -q` | 35 passed; includes FP16/BF16 native-byte parity, ownership, padding and empty input |
| `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_qk_norm_rope.py -q` | 21 passed; decode preservation, exclusions, BF16/FP16 changing-input graphs |
| `python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_qknorm.py -k two_rows -xq` | 3 existing standalone half-warp equivalence regressions passed |
| `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --error-exitcode 99 python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_table_qk_norm_rope.py -k hybrid -xq` | 7 passed; 0 errors |
| Same selected cases under `compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck --error-exitcode 99` | 7 passed; 0 errors |
| `python -m pytest test/registered/unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py -q` | 104 tests and 2 subtests passed |

**Fresh compatible-serving validation:** one H200, TP1, SGLang v0.5.20 serving paths, Torch `2.13.0.2+cu130`, Triton `3.8.0`, FlashInfer `0.6.18`, and kernel `0.4.7.0+cu130`. The QKV producer, cached NeoX RoPE and attention consumer paths used by these cases were checked; the exact PR CUDA/shared-normalization files from `01b927b` were loaded through a compatibility adapter. The CUDA header SHA256 is `eb5c6486fdfd265bf8aa9a54ea52be72ce126516f50802b747ea951e4bf430e0`. The comparison uses optimized #45214 standalone normalization in the baseline and preserves identical original decode treatment in both arms.

Paired real-model smoke outputs are exact at **128, 4096 and 8192 input tokens** for Qwen3-4B BF16/FA3 and Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B FP16/FlashInfer. A direct compatible-runtime FP16/BF16 contract check also matches Q/K exactly, with Q input/V unchanged, K updated and contiguous Q.

Paired Qwen3-4B **GSM8K-200 with sgl-eval 0.1.3**:

| Arm | Correct | Errors | Truncations |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Optimized split baseline | 188/200 (94%) | 0 | 0 |
| PR CUDA hybrid | 188/200 (94%) | 0 | 0 |

The same 200 questions, expected answers, generation texts and per-question grades match exactly. The existing verified canonical corpus was reused; no prompts, grading or tolerances were changed.

Checkpoints:

- `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` revision `1cfa9a7208912126459214e8b04321603b3df60c`
- `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` revision `97b0c614be4d77ee51c0cef4e5f07c00f9eb65b3`

Accuracy command/settings (`MODEL` is the verified local snapshot of the pinned checkpoint):

```bash
sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:31122/v1 \
  --model "$MODEL" --num-examples 200 --num-threads 1 \
  --max-tokens 2048 --temperature 0 --top-p 1 --seed 42 \
  --no-thinking --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=false \
  --out-dir "$OUTPUT_DIR"
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

**Fresh compatible-serving comparison:** baseline A1 → candidate B → baseline A2, with fresh servers, identical checkpoint/runtime/seed/cache/chunking/graph settings, and **200 measured requests per window at concurrency 4** after warmup. This is six server phases and nine serving windows, not a repeat of the broader candidate matrix. All **1800 measured requests completed without errors**.

For each metric, the baseline below is the arithmetic mean of A1 and A2's window metric. Change is `100 * (B / mean(A1, A2) - 1)`; these are descriptive bracketed comparisons, not confidence intervals or pooled percentiles.

| Workload | p50 change | p95 change | p99 change | Completed requests/s change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-4B BF16/FA3, 4096 input / 1 output | -2.39% | -2.75% | -2.93% | +2.27% |
| Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B FP16/FlashInfer, 4096 input | -3.70% | -1.47% | -2.89% | +3.65% |
| Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B FP16/FlashInfer, 8192 input control | -1.69% | -1.59% | -1.76% | +1.86% |

Absolute per-window latency:

| Workload | A1 p50 ms | B p50 ms | A2 p50 ms | A1 p95 ms | B p95 ms | A2 p95 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-4B 4096→1 | 251.470 | 245.000 | 250.533 | 256.680 | 249.602 | 256.639 |
| Embedding 4096 | 55.062 | 52.898 | 54.794 | 56.167 | 55.252 | 55.986 |
| Embedding 8192 | 160.953 | 157.954 | 160.397 | 163.223 | 160.947 | 163.859 |

Generation latency is the **complete non-streaming HTTP request through response-body read/JSON parse with one generated token**: a one-token request-latency/TTFT proxy, not first-streamed-token TTFT. Embedding latency is complete embedding response latency. Throughput is completed requests per second over each measured window.

<details>
<summary>Serving reproduction protocol</summary>

For an independent source-pair reproduction, compare base `b50d4394945d3dcacea05ee4afd334a9b225cbdc` with PR `01b927b0ba6992c18b6dd185f0490ff528eeb0fe` on one Hopper GPU. Enable the existing flag in both source trees; use the pinned model revisions above. The recorded compatible-v0.5.20 measurements use the adapter described above, so these source-pair instructions specify the workload rather than package that adapter.

Common launch settings in every arm:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL" --dtype "$DTYPE" --attention-backend "$BACKEND" \
  --enable-fused-qk-norm-rope \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31122 --tp-size 1 --random-seed 42 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \
  --max-total-tokens 196608 --max-running-requests 64 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7 --log-level warning \
  --cuda-graph-config '{"prefill":{"backend":"breakable","bs":[1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384,32768],"max_bs":32768},"decode":{"backend":"full","bs":[1,2,4,8,16,32],"max_bs":32}}'
```

For Qwen3-4B use `DTYPE=bfloat16`, `BACKEND=fa3`, and append `--return-hidden-states-mode last`. For Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B use `DTYPE=float16`, `BACKEND=flashinfer`, and append `--is-embedding`. Use local model snapshots with offline Hugging Face/Transformers access and only one visible GPU.

The HTTP client uses explicit token IDs, not tokenizer-generated random text:

```python
def ids(length, seed):
    return [1000 + (i * 13 + seed * 79) % 3000 for i in range(length)]
```

- **Generation:** `POST /generate` with `input_ids=ids(4096, seed)`, `sampling_params={"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 1, "ignore_eos": True}`, `return_logprob=True`, and `return_hidden_states="last"`. Hidden-state/logprob response serialization is included in the measured latency.
- **Embedding:** `POST /v1/embeddings` with one token-ID array in `input=ids(length, seed)` and `encoding_format="float"`; measure lengths 4096 and 8192 separately.
- **Order/cache:** fresh servers in A1 -> B -> A2 order for each model/configuration. Before each window issue eight concurrent warmups with seeds `700 + i` (`i=0..7`), wait for all eight, then `POST /flush_cache?timeout=60` once. Read that response as text, not JSON. Submit 200 measured requests with seeds `1000 + i` (`i=0..199`) through a semaphore of four, with no flush between requests.
- **Timing:** after acquiring the semaphore, start the request timer immediately before the HTTP POST; validate status, read the complete response body as text and JSON-decode it before stopping. Client semaphore queue time is excluded. Compute percentiles over the 200 successful request times. A separate wall timer surrounds submission/completion of all 200 requests; throughput is `200 / wall_seconds`.

`bench_serving --disable-stream` reproduces the non-streaming timing class, but ordinary `random-ids` mode does not guarantee the same IDs, diagnostic fields or JSON-read boundary. Use the explicit HTTP protocol above when matching this workload.

</details>


**Untimed actual-server profiles** confirm `qk_norm_rope_kernel` engagement in the candidate:

| Profiled workload | Baseline GPU kernels | Candidate GPU kernels | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-4B | 2081 | 2009 | 72 |
| Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B | 364 | 308 | 56 |

The activation-dtype Q-copy kernel family disappears; other copy kernels remain. Native decode normalization remains in the generation candidate trace. Separate current-source preparation profiles show **three preparation kernels → one**, with no `aten::contiguous` in the hybrid path. D128 BF16/FP16 int32/int64 specializations compile with **56 registers and zero spills** on SM90a. Profiles are untimed engagement/copy-removal evidence and are not mixed into serving measurements.

**Current-source cold-L2 preparation microbenchmark:** `python test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_qk_norm_rope.py` passed all six token/dtype shapes. At 4096 tokens, 32 Q heads / 8 KV heads / D128, split norm + cached RoPE + Q conversion measured **79.456 → 33.455 us (BF16)** and **79.331 → 31.787 us (FP16)**. The marker framework rotates inputs to defeat L2 reuse.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
- [x] Local code review completed.

Ruff 0.15.1, isort 7.0.0, clang-format 20.1.7, registered-test admission, pytest entrypoint lint and `git diff --check` passed. Repository pre-commit checks passed for all 10 contribution files with `pre-commit run --show-diff-on-failure --files $(git diff --name-only b50d439..HEAD)`; no files were changed. Both local Claude and Copilot GPT complete-diff reviewers covered all 10 files and returned no actionable findings; contribution code remains at the reviewed `01b927b`.

Final audit reran the 7 hybrid cases, 21 model dispatch/graph cases and 3 shared half-warp regressions: all 31 passed without code changes. Renewed complete-diff Standards and Spec/functionality reviews returned no actionable findings. Base CI currently stops at the draft gate ("PR is draft. Blocking CI."); this is not a GPU-test failure or a CI pass.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

Implementation and local validation were assisted by GitHub Copilot; automated authorship is disclosed in the commit trailer.

<!-- mintlify-fork-preview-approval -->
### Preview approval required

This pull request comes from a fork, so Mintlify won't build a preview until someone with write access approves commit `b1a2b65`.

[Approve preview](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47785/checks?check_run_id=126467902159)

Fixed the unrelated CI failure - Inkling checkpoint replay fixture in d6f3d18e2dfab947c242414177386706598aec89. After #47173, the draft graph runner reads `backend.cache_loc_dtype` instead of returning a fixed `torch.int64`. The fixture still returned a bare `Mock()`, so real buffer allocation failed with `TypeError: ones(): argument 'dtype' must be torch.dtype, not Mock`. This is an upstream test-fixture mismatch, unrelated to the Qwen3 fusion changes.

The open fix #47858 addresses this by setting `cache_loc_dtype=torch.int64` on the mock backend. I reused that exact one-line test correction here so this PR is not blocked by the same fixture error. Production code, capture/replay assertions, and parameter combinations are unchanged. Since the fixture edit is identical, it is expected to merge cleanly when the upstream fix lands; any intervening changes still need to be checked at merge time.

Python syntax, the isolated before/after mock dtype contract check, and `git diff --check` passed locally. Full GPU replay validation remains for CI: this local environment has no PyTorch/CUDA, and pre-commit is unavailable.

<!-- pr-check-comment runs=41592788197 -->
Required checks failed on f0cc5cc; this PR cannot be merged until they pass.

**Lint** ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41592788197))
Run `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and push the result. The run log shows any other failing step.
@BBuf Base CI passed. Can you help take a look?? Thank you!

Applied the exact one-line Arm64 test fix proposed in #48223 in commit 093cf61e1d74644627d6d7dcb42d1f5cde1b784c to address the unrelated CI regression tracked in #48221.

`test/registered/cpu/arm64/test_moe.py` now explicitly imports `sgl_kernel` so its `torch.ops.sgl_kernel` operators are registered before use. The test no longer depends on the transitive import side effect removed by #47731. This is the only change in this commit; the Qwen3 fusion, eligibility, kernel implementation and numerical behavior are unchanged.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

```bash
  --model-path "$MODEL" --dtype "$DTYPE" --attention-backend "$BACKEND" \
  --enable-fused-qk-norm-rope \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31122 --tp-size 1 --random-seed 42 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \
  --max-total-tokens 196608 --max-running-requests 64 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7 --log-level warning \
  --cuda-graph-config '{"prefill":{"backend":"breakable","bs":[1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384,32768],"max_bs":32768},"decode":{"backend":"full","bs":[1,2,4,8,16,32],"max_bs":32}}'
```

For Qwen3-4B use `DTYPE=bfloat16`, `BACKEND=fa3`, and append `--return-hidden-states-mode last`. For Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B use `DTYPE=float16`, `BACKEND=flashinfer`, and append `--is-embedding`. Use local model snapshots with offline Hugging Face/Transformers access and only one visible GPU.

The HTTP client uses explicit token IDs, not tokenizer-generated random text:

```python
def ids(length, seed):
    return [1000 + (i * 13 + seed * 79) % 3000 for i in range(length)]
```

- **Generation:** `POST /generate` with `input_ids=ids(4096, seed)`, `sampling_params={"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 1, "ignore_eos": True}`, `return_logprob=True`, and `return_hidden_states="last"`. Hidden-state/logprob response serialization is included in the measured latency.
- **Embedding:** `POST /v1/embeddings` with one token-ID array in `input=ids(length, seed)` and `encoding_format="float"`; measure lengths 4096 and 8192 separately.
- **Order/cache:** fresh servers in A1 -> B -> A2 order for each model/configuration. Before each window issue eight concurrent warmups with seeds `700 + i` (`i=0..7`), wait for all eight, then `POST /flush_cache?timeout=60` once. Read that response as text, not JSON. Submit 200 measured requests with seeds `1000 + i` (`i=0..199`) through a semaphore of four, with no flush between requests.
- **Timing:** after acquiring the semaphore, start the request timer immediately before the HTTP POST; validate status, read the complete response body as text and JSON-decode it before stopping. Client semaphore queue time is excluded. Compute percentiles over the 200 successful request times. A separate wall timer surrounds submission/completion of all 200 requests; throughput is `200 / wall_seconds`.

`bench_serving --disable-stream` reproduces the non-streaming timing class, but ordinary `random-ids` mode does not guarantee the same IDs, diagnostic fields or JSON-read boundary. Use the explicit HTTP protocol above when matching this workload.

</details>


**Untimed actual-server profiles** confirm `qk_norm_rope_kernel` engagement in the candidate:

| Profiled workload | Baseline GPU kernels | Candidate GPU kernels | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-4B | 2081 | 2009 | 72 |
| Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B | 364 | 308 | 56 |

The activation-dtype Q-copy kernel family disappears; other copy kernels remain. Native decode normalization remains in the generation candidate trace. Separate current-source preparation profiles show **three preparation kernels → one**, with no `aten::contiguous` in the hybrid path. D128 BF16/FP16 int32/int64 specializations compile with **56 registers and zero spills** on SM90a. Profiles are untimed engagement/copy-removal evidence and are not mixed into serving measurements.

**Current-source cold-L2 preparation microbenchmark:** `python test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_qk_norm_rope.py` passed all six token/dtype shapes. At 4096 tokens, 32 Q heads / 8 KV heads / D128, split norm + cached RoPE + Q conversion measured **79.456 → 33.455 us (BF16)** and **79.331 → 31.787 us (FP16)**. The marker framework rotates inputs to defeat L2 reuse.

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import (
+    cache_once,
+    is_arch_support_pdl,
+    load_jit,
+    make_cpp_args,
+)
+from sglang.srt.utils.custom_op import register_custom_op
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from tvm_ffi.module import Module
+
+
+@cache_once
+def _module(dtype: torch.dtype, head_dim: int) -> Module:
+    if dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16) or head_dim not in (64, 128, 256):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "qk_norm_rope requires FP16/BF16 and head dimension 64/128/256"
+        )
+    args = make_cpp_args(dtype, head_dim, is_arch_support_pdl())
+    return load_jit(
+        "qk_norm_rope",
+        *args,
+        cuda_files=["attention/qk_norm_rope.cuh"],
+        cuda_wrappers=[("run", f"qk_norm_rope<{args}>")],
+    )
+
+
+@register_custom_op(mutates_args=["k", "out"])
+def _qk_norm_rope_out(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    k: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    q_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    k_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    cos_sin_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    head_dim: int,
+    eps: float,
+) -> None:
+    _module(q.dtype, head_dim).run(
+        q.view(q.shape[0], q.shape[1] // head_dim, head_dim),
+        k.view(k.shape[0], k.shape[1] // head_dim, head_dim),
+        out.view(out.shape[0], out.shape[1] // head_dim, head_dim),
+        q_weight,
+        k_weight,
+        cos_sin_cache,
+        positions,
+        eps,
+    )
+
+
+def qk_norm_rope(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    k: torch.Tensor,
+    q_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    k_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    cos_sin_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    head_dim: int,
+    eps: float,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Cached full-head NeoX RoPE after QK RMSNorm, for FP16/BF16 CUDA tensors.
+
+    Returns a separate contiguous Q; modifies K in its original storage and
+    leaves Q unchanged. Q/K are [tokens, heads * head_dim] with aligned row
+    strides and contiguous columns. Weights have the activation dtype, the
+    table is contiguous FP32, and int32/int64 positions index valid table rows.
+    Q/K may share packed QKV storage, but their elements must not overlap.
+    Normalized values are rounded before rotation, as in separate CUDA kernels.
+    """
+    out = torch.empty(q.shape, dtype=q.dtype, device=q.device)
+    _qk_norm_rope_out(
+        q, k, out, q_weight, k_weight, cos_sin_cache, positions, head_dim, eps
+    )
+    return out

+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.benchmark import marker
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.qk_norm_rope import qk_norm_rope
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.rope import apply_rope_inplace
+from sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.norm import fused_inplace_qknorm
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(
+    est_time=6, stage="base-b-kernel-benchmark", runner_config="1-gpu-large"
+)
+
+
+def prepare(qkv, qw, kw, cache, positions, fused):
+    q, k, _ = qkv.split([32 * 128, 8 * 128, 8 * 128], dim=-1)
+    if fused:
+        return qk_norm_rope(q, k, qw, kw, cache, positions, 128, 1e-6)
+    q = q.view(q.shape[0], 32, 128)
+    k = k.view(k.shape[0], 8, 128)
+    fused_inplace_qknorm(q, k, qw, kw, 1e-6)
+    apply_rope_inplace(q, k, cache, positions, is_neox=True)
+    return q.contiguous()
+
+
+@marker.parametrize("tokens", [512, 4096, 8192], [512, 4096])
+@marker.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])

<!-- mintlify-fork-preview-approval -->
### Preview approval required

This pull request comes from a fork, so Mintlify won't build a preview until someone with write access approves commit `b1a2b65`.

[Approve preview](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47785/checks?check_run_id=126467902159)

Fixed the unrelated CI failure - Inkling checkpoint replay fixture in d6f3d18e2dfab947c242414177386706598aec89. After #47173, the draft graph runner reads `backend.cache_loc_dtype` instead of returning a fixed `torch.int64`. The fixture still returned a bare `Mock()`, so real buffer allocation failed with `TypeError: ones(): argument 'dtype' must be torch.dtype, not Mock`. This is an upstream test-fixture mismatch, unrelated to the Qwen3 fusion changes.

The open fix #47858 addresses this by setting `cache_loc_dtype=torch.int64` on the mock backend. I reused that exact one-line test correction here so this PR is not blocked by the same fixture error. Production code, capture/replay assertions, and parameter combinations are unchanged. Since the fixture edit is identical, it is expected to merge cleanly when the upstream fix lands; any intervening changes still need to be checked at merge time.

Python syntax, the isolated before/after mock dtype contract check, and `git diff --check` passed locally. Full GPU replay validation remains for CI: this local environment has no PyTorch/CUDA, and pre-commit is unavailable.
